question.text: Under the SCORES framework, once an entity receives an intimation from SEBI on an investor complaint, by when must it resolve the complaint?

answer.text: Within 21 days of receiving the SEBI intimation; failure to resolve investor complaints can otherwise attract penalty or suspension
There is no specified timeframe for resolving SCORES complaints
Within 90 days only if the investor escalates a second time
Only at the end of the financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook explains that investor complaints under the SCORES portal must be resolved within 21 days of receiving SEBI's intimation. Separately, the Stock Broker Regulations allow SEBI to impose penalty or suspension on a broker who fails to redress investor complaints. The Trap: Saying that no timeframe exists, or pegging the timeline to a yearly cycle, contradicts the SCORES 21-day rule. Specific per-day monetary amounts are not the workbook-stated remedy and should not be assumed. Note: Two anchors to remember: SCORES timeline = 21 days from SEBI intimation; consequence for non-redressal = penalty or suspension under the Stock Broker Regulations.
